lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.unitTitle: Kitchen Skills and Flexible Meal Planning
lessonRef.title: Explicit model: knife and heat boundaries

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic knife and heat boundaries task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: A trusted adult walks the learner through the real kitchen, pointing to the knives normally used there, the stove, and the oven, and states out loud the household's specific boundary for each: what the learner may already do alone, what requires the adult standing right there, and what is off-limits for now.
safetyNotes: Knives are held and used only the way the adult demonstrates, blade always pointed away from fingers and body, and are never carried around while walking or handed to anyone unsupervised.
The stove and oven are only turned on, adjusted, or reached into with the adult physically present for this lesson; the learner does not operate either one alone yet.
Stop the activity immediately and tell the adult right away for any cut, burn, or other injury, no matter how small it seems.

simulationAlternative.description: If there is no real kitchen, knife, or stove available to walk through, the learner instead reviews a provided printed list of common kitchen scenarios involving knives and heat and sorts each one into 'may do alone,' 'only with an adult present,' or 'not allowed yet,' explaining the reasoning for three of the sorts.

materials: adult-or-local: the household's real knives normally used for food preparation
adult-or-local: the household's real stove and oven
learner-local: paper or a notes app for recording boundaries

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g7-u03-l02-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g7-u03-l02-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g7-u03-l02-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g7-u03-l02-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Explain, using one specific task from your sort, what could go wrong if that boundary were ignored, and why the adult's presence specifically changes the risk for that task.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g7-u03-l02-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g7-u03-l02-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g7-u03-l02-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Boundary accuracy: Boundaries for at least two real knives, the stove, and the oven are recorded accurately and match what the adult stated. | Reasoning about risk: The learner explains a specific, plausible reason a named boundary exists, tied to a real task. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g7-u03-l02-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner ask the adult about one specific kitchen injury or near-miss the adult remembers, and identify which boundary, if it had been followed, would have prevented it.

resources.title: knife and heat boundaries worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: A trusted adult walks the learner through the real kitchen, pointing to the knives normally used there, the stove, and the oven, and states out loud the household's specific boundary for each: what the learner may already do alone, what requires the adult standing right there, and what is off-limits for now.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact knife and heat boundaries decision or action.
Model move 2: Before the walkthrough, write down what you currently think you are and are not allowed to do with knives or the stove in your home.
Model move 3: With your adult present, walk through the real kitchen and record the specific boundary they state for each item.

Model check: Boundary accuracy: Boundaries for at least two real knives, the stove, and the oven are recorded accurately and match what the adult stated. | Reasoning about risk: The learner explains a specific, plausible reason a named boundary exists, tied to a real task.

resources.title: knife and heat boundaries action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for knife and heat boundaries.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: knife and heat boundaries coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: A trusted adult walks the learner through the real kitchen, pointing to the knives normally used there, the stove, and the oven, and states out loud the household's specific boundary for each: what the learner may already do alone, what requires the adult standing right there, and what is off-limits for now.
Coach direction: Before the walkthrough, write down what you currently think you are and are not allowed to do with knives or the stove in your home.
Learner prompt: List one knife task and one stove or oven task you currently believe you are allowed to do alone.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: knife and heat boundaries complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: With your adult present, walk through the real kitchen and record the specific boundary they state for each item.
Response 1 (t2-p1): For at least two real knives used in the household, I recorded whether I may use each alone, only with the adult present, or not yet.
Response 2 (t2-p2): For the stove and for the oven, I recorded the specific boundary the adult stated for each.
Response 3 (t2-p3): I repeated each boundary back to the adult in my own words and they confirmed I understood it correctly.

Equal-access rule: If there is no real kitchen, knife, or stove available to walk through, the learner instead reviews a provided printed list of common kitchen scenarios involving knives and heat and sorts each one into 'may do alone,' 'only with an adult present,' or 'not allowed yet,' explaining the reasoning for three of the sorts.

resources.title: knife and heat boundaries minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Explain, using one specific task from your sort, what could go wrong if that boundary were ignored, and why the adult's presence specifically changes the risk for that task.

Success checks: Boundary accuracy: Boundaries for at least two real knives, the stove, and the oven are recorded accurately and match what the adult stated. | Reasoning about risk: The learner explains a specific, plausible reason a named boundary exists, tied to a real task.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: knife and heat boundaries supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g7-u03-l02-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g7-u03-l02-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional knife and heat boundaries condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Boundary accuracy: Boundaries for at least two real knives, the stove, and the oven are recorded accurately and match what the adult stated. | Reasoning about risk: The learner explains a specific, plausible reason a named boundary exists, tied to a real task..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g7-u03-l02-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guardianInvolvement.role: Give permission; provide only the supervision, handling, review, or observation named in the lesson; attest only that the physical event occurred.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
